1.4.0.title: Themes
1.4.0.text: Pick a dark and a light theme in Settings → Appearance: Fork’s own, Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Rosé Pine, Nord, Gruvbox, GitHub or Vesper. Hover one to try it first.

1.4.0.title: Undo when you close something
1.4.0.text: Closing a terminal or workspace doesn’t ask any more. Undo puts it back, still running; after that, ⌘⇧T opens it again in the same folder.

1.4.0.title: Fork moves like a Mac app
1.4.0.text: The sidebar and panel slide, splits grow out of the terminal they came from, and you can drag your workspaces into any order.

1.4.0.title: Needs you sounds different
1.4.0.text: Two soft knocks when something is waiting for you, so you can tell it from the done chime without looking.

1.3.1.title: Safer with downloaded projects
1.3.1.text: Fork never types a name with hidden characters into your terminal, and git never runs programs a project brings along. Pages in Fork see only their own folder.

1.3.1.title: Terminal text stays sharp
1.3.1.text: If your Mac’s graphics restart while Fork is open, terminals redraw cleanly instead of losing letters.

1.3.0.title: Fork in the menu bar
1.3.0.text: Click the fork at the top of your screen, from any app, to see every workspace and what needs you. Its square fills in while something’s waiting on you.

1.3.0.title: Fork knows when Claude needs you
1.3.0.text: When Claude stops to ask your OK or a question, its workspace turns yellow and says what it’s asking, even on the tab you’re in.

1.3.0.title: Each chat comes back
1.3.0.text: Reopen Fork and every Claude terminal picks up its own chat, not the same one in all of them.

1.3.0.title: Smooth scrolling in Claude
1.3.0.text: In Claude’s fullscreen view, the chat follows your trackpad or mouse row by row instead of jumping.

1.3.0.title: ⌘K is back
1.3.0.text: ⌘K opens the command palette again: say what you want in plain words. Search your files with ⌘⇧F.
